To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the extent of sensitisation to relevant inhaled allergens influences asthma severity in adulthood, whereas the extent of bronchial responsiveness does not.
the extent of sensitisation to relevant perennial allergens significantly influences asthma severity and bronchial hyper-responsiveness but not lung function outcome in asthmatic children and adults.
the extent of sensitisation to furred animals is a major determinant of clinical asthma severity and bronchial responsiveness in adult life.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the long-term outcome of childhood asthma in terms of lung function, airway responsiveness, and asthma severity.
a better understanding of the natural history of asthma and the mechanisms of its progression.
the course and outcome of the airway obstruction in asthmatic children over a period of 30 years, and with the factors influencing this course.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the course of lung function in asthma is influenced by gender and initial lung function, but not by asthma severity, and that the outcome is worse in females than in asthmatic boys.
the course of lung function in asthma from childhood to adulthood is influenced by initial lung function, gender, and the extent of bronchial responsiveness.
asthma severity in childhood is a poor prognostic factor for adult asthma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
asthma in adulthood is characterized by a high degree of airway responsiveness to inhaled allergens, and by a high asthma severity.

the extent of sensitisation is the major factor influencing the outcome of asthma severity and airway responsiveness, whereas the outcome of lung function is determined by the extent of sensitising allergens, gender, and initial lung function.
asthma in childhood is more severe and persistent in girls than in boys.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the course of asthma from childhood to adulthood is not uniform.
asthma in childhood is not a benign disease, and it is not a transient disease.
the course of lung function in childhood asthma is not necessarily associated with asthma severity or sensitisation to furred animals.
